## What the chronicles say [Record]

The captured prisoner who walked out of the Order's capital is one of the better-attested episodes of the century. [Kęstutis](../characters/kestutis.qmd), over sixty, and Algirdas had taken Eckersberg and Johannisburg; a small band of knights returning from another raid fell on his camp by [Lake Ublik (Wobel)](../places/lake_ublik.qmd) in Masuria. Wigand dates the [capture](ev_kestutis_captured_1361.qmd) **21 March 1361** (Wartberge: 13 March). He was held at Marienburg about half a year and escaped on **11 November 1361** (Baronas: around 11 or 17–18 November) with the help of **Alfas (Adolfas)**, a servant of Lithuanian origin, who removed bricks from the cell wall over months and carried out the rubble; Kęstutis broke through the wall, crossed the empty terrace, dropped into the dry moat where Alfas waited with horses and a Teutonic knight's cloak, and rode out through the outer gate as a knight, toward Liebstadt; he hid in a bog, freed the horses and went on foot over the Drwęca to Mazovia. Alfas's fate is not recorded. The main source is Wigand of Marburg, whose chronicle survives only through a Latin translation and fragments; Baronas (2004) notes that Wigand knew details only a participant could. See Baronas, "Kęstučio pabėgimas iš Marienburgo" (Lietuvos istorijos studijos), and Wikipedia, Kęstutis.

## What really happened [Saga]

No magic. In the consecrated cellars [Birutė](../characters/birute.qmd)'s amber bead goes cold (Kalba cannot reach into a consecrated place) and the Order lets him keep it. The escape is wit and loyalty: Kniprode, Grand Master for ten years, offers freedom for baptism and Kęstutis, bound by his thunder-mark, cannot promise what he will not keep. The invented young brother [Hohenstein](../characters/hohenstein.qmd) (the third knight who took him at Ublik; not the real Osterode komtur) carries his meals and translates; the young wolf Jonas, taken in the same column, kills a sergeant at the last gate and takes his Christian name (saga). Alfas's fate is left open. It becomes the template for his son's escape in 1382.

## Consequences

Caused by [the capture at Lake Ublik](ev_kestutis_captured_1361.qmd). The graph attaches no outgoing 'causes' edge. The escape is the pattern [Vytautas](../characters/vytautas.qmd) repeats at [Krėva](ev_kreva_escape.qmd) twenty-one years later (Kęstutis tells it to him at Krėva, Book I ch. 8).

## Dramatisation

Book VI ch. 16 "Paimtas" (Kęstutis; March 1361, Lake Ublik), ch. 17 "Marienburgo Požemis" (Kniprode; September), ch. 18 "Alfo Raktas" (Jonas; 11 November 1361, the eve of the saga's Vėlinės mood). Told again by Kęstutis to Vytautas in Book I ch. 8 (the wall dug out, the white knight's mantle, the horses).
